title: Addressing social problems adequately in a network – Digital case management of integrated care of general practitioners' patients' social problems
summary:
General practitioners are often the first point of contact for patients with various physical, psychological, and social problems that can negatively affect health. At present, suitable structures are lacking to digitally record and specifically address, in particular, patients’ social problems and needs.
The SOPRAN study addresses this and pursues the goal of informing general practitioners about social service providers and enabling them to digitally refer general practice patients. The physical, psychological, and social needs of general practice patients are recorded using a screening questionnaire in the SOPRAN patient app. Based on the results, general practitioners can select appropriate medical and non-medical contact points in the digital interface and provide patients with the corresponding contact information in the SOPRAN app. Alternatively, the general practitioners can establish contact with the Disabled Community Bonn (BG) for further counseling.
The primary goal of the SOPRAN study is to evaluate the acceptance, user-friendliness, and feasibility of the SOPRAN intervention. For this purpose, the intervention will be tested by general practitioners, patients, and social workers of the BG in a two-stage mixed-methods study.
conditions: Factors influencing health status and contact with health services

interventions.name: General practice patients with bio-psycho-social needs receive individualized contact information for social support services via the SOPRAN app.
General practice patients without bio-psycho-social needs receive care as usual.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients: GP patients, ≥ 18 years old, statutory or private insurance, smart device use ≥ 3 times a week

Doctors: general practicioner

Behindertengemeinschaft Bonn (BG): social worker at BG
Exclusion criteria:
Patients: no internet access

Doctors: no internet access
